drivingQuestion: Is the second clause redundant with the first?

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ הַיְינוּ רֵישָׁא: אָבִיהָ וּבַעְלָהּ מְפִירִין נְדָרֶיהָ! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: אוֹ אָבִיהָ אוֹ בַעְלָהּ קָתָנֵי, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The mishna states that if the father nullified her vow and the husband did not nullify it, or if the husband nullified it and the father did not nullify it, then the vow is not nullified. The Gemara asks: «Is this» not the same as «the first clause» of the mishna, which states: «Her father and her husband nullify her vows?» The Gemara answers: The second clause is necessary, «lest you say:» The mishna «is teaching» that «either her father or her husband» can nullify her vows, but there is no need for both of them to do so, which is also a possible interpretation of the Hebrew phrase used. Therefore, the mishna «teaches us» that it means that both of them must nullify the vow.
